activities.anchor: Imagine a future archaeologist digging up your household's bin
activities.caption: read your own bin the way she would
activities.name: arcBinBuckets

config.prompt: A future archaeologist excavates your bin from this week. File each observation by what it actually tells her:

items.label: packaging reveals what you ate and where it came from
repair receipts reveal what you think worth mending
the ratio of wrappers to fresh-food scraps
no nappies, no pet food, no beer bottles — absences

config.why: Even what is absent speaks. Each absence is a fact about your household — and she would know all this from things you never thought of as messages at all.

activities.anchor: Digging is controlled, recorded destruction
activities.caption: bet on the consequence of one rule
activities.name: arcDestructionPredict

config.q: Excavation is controlled, recorded destruction — you cannot re-dig a layer. Which practice follows most directly from that single fact?
choices: Dig every threatened site as fast as possible before anything is lost
Survey first and dig only where justified, because the record taken must outlast the site
Prefer spectacular objects so the dig is worth the loss
Store the soil for later re-deposition so the site can be rebuilt
config.why: Everything in the lesson follows from this: recording standards, archives and publication are as much a part of the science as trowels — and the choice not to dig comes first.

activities.anchor: revealing earthworks no surveyor ever walked
activities.caption: pair each survey method with what it detects
activities.name: arcSurveyMatch

config.prompt: Survey maps what is there before any shovel. Match each method to its target:

pairs.right: buried walls, by their effect on soil moisture
ditches, hearths and kilns, by their magnetism
earthworks under forest canopy, stripped in software

config.why: The hazard is that excavation destroys the site, so survey does the work that survives: it maps what is there and it maps what is worth the irreplaceable cost of digging.

activities.anchor: Finally comes inference
activities.caption: order the layers, bottom to top
activities.name: arcStratOrder

config.prompt: Stratigraphy accumulates oldest-first. Put these units of a site's life in depositional order:
items: A floor is laid and occupied
Ashes from the hearth fall and settle on the floor
A wall collapses and its rubble buries the ash
Later digging cuts a pit through all three
config.why: Each layer is a unit of time containing a moment of a site's life. The Harris matrix formalises the stack of cut-and-fill relationships into one sequence — the site's history, in diagram form.

activities.anchor: survive only in special conditions
activities.caption: file each bias in the record
activities.name: arcBiasBuckets

config.prompt: The record is skewed, and honest archaeology begins by admitting it. File each bias:

items.label: wood, cloth and basketry survive only waterlogged, frozen or very dry
elite burials dominate the spectacular finds
speech, law and song left no objects
the surviving past over-represents stone, bone, pottery and fired clay

config.why: The formation processes that created the record — discard, burial, erosion, later digging — are themselves objects of study.

activities.anchor: It is a probability range, not a single year
activities.caption: guess the range of the carbon clock
activities.name: arcRadiocarbonEstimate

config.prompt: Radiocarbon covers organic material back about how many years?
config.why: About 50,000 years, with a stated uncertainty — resolved by calibration curves built from tree rings, because atmospheric carbon-14 has not been constant.
config.context: Beyond that, different clocks take over: potassium–argon for early hominin sites, luminescence for when sediment was last exposed to light. Every good excavation reports several independent dates for the same layers.

activities.anchor:
the first evidence-based
    framework for prehistory
activities.caption: the discipline's own stratigraphy
activities.name: arcDisciplineTimeline

events.label: Thomsen's Three Age System
events.text: The Copenhagen museum's collection ordered into Stone, Bronze and Iron from find associations — the first evidence-based framework for prehistory.

events.label: Schliemann's trench at Troy
events.text: He found Homer's city and cut straight through the strata that made it meaningful; the modern instinct — record everything, destroy nothing — was written partly in reaction.

events.label: Radiocarbon dating
events.text: Libby's method dated organic material directly, freeing prehistory from guesswork and overturning chronologies built on cross-dating.

events.label: Processual archaeology
events.text: Binford demanded archaeology behave like science: state hypotheses about past systems and test them.

events.label: The post-processual response
events.text: Hodder answered that past people were makers of meaning — symbols, agency and the archaeologist's own position belong in the interpretation.

activities.anchor: opened the ship-mound at Sutton Hoo
activities.caption: find the faulty line in the Sutton Hoo story
activities.name: arcSuttonHooSpot

config.prompt: A student writes up Sutton Hoo as evidence for the method. One line is wrong — find it.
lines: In 1939 Basil Brown opened the ship-mound at Sutton Hoo and found an undisturbed Anglo-Saxon burial chamber.
Everything that makes it science rather than spectacle came from the associations.
The gold buckle, helmet and Byzantine silver are what dated the burial and proved the kingdom's reach.
The coins dated the burial to the early seventh century.
Frankish coins, Swedish helmet parallels and Mediterranean silver turned a treasure into an argument about trade and politics at the edge of written history.
config.correction: The coins dated it, and the reach of the grave-goods across three material traditions proved the kingdom's trade — not the individual precious objects.
config.why: Context, not the object, is what gets preserved. This is why the field treats treasure hunting as the opposite of its method — an unprovenanced find is evidence largely destroyed.

activities.anchor: The shape changed
activities.caption: drag between flat and folded
activities.name: archPaperCompare

config.prompt: The same sheet of paper, twice. Drag the divider.

before.label: flat sheet across two books
before.text: Bending carries the load. One face stretches in tension, the other squeezes in compression, and the sagging coin slides off. The material is fine; the shape is doing no work.

after.label: pleated or rolled into a tube
after.text: The coin sits easily. Depth in the direction of bending is what resists bending — the fold moves material away from the neutral axis where it could do nothing.

config.why: Nothing about the material changed; the shape changed, and with it the strength. Strength is not only what something is made of, but how its shape lets forces flow through it.

activities.anchor: An arch carries the same load
activities.caption: file each structural character by how it carries
activities.name: archCarryBuckets

config.prompt: Two structural characters run the entire subject. File each by how it carries load:

items.label: a beam — one face stretches, the other squeezes
an arch — every stone pushes on its neighbour
a pointed Gothic rib
a steel truss member

config.why: The distinction matters because materials have preferences. Stone is strong in compression and weak in tension — which is why the Romans, who had no steel, built arches that still stand two thousand years later.

activities.anchor: curve called a catenary
activities.caption: find the faulty line in the catenary argument
activities.name: archCatenarySpot

config.prompt: A student explains Hooke's inversion. One line is wrong — find it.
lines: A hanging chain droops into a catenary, carrying its own weight in pure tension.
Robert Hooke described the trick in 1675, hiding the wording as an anagram to keep the credit.
Flip the curve upside down and the pure pulling becomes pure pushing: an arch with zero bending.
The parabola is the same curve by a different name, so a catenary and a parabola can be used interchangeably at any span.
For shallow arches the two shapes nearly coincide, which is why the difference confuses even engineers.
config.correction: The parabola is a cousin, not the same curve: it is correct when weight is spread evenly ALONG THE SPAN (a bridge deck), while a catenary matches weight carried along the curve itself.
config.why: The catenary climbs slightly steeper toward the ends, where the parabola stays shallower. Nearly identical for shallow arches — which is exactly why the difference is easy to miss and important to know.

activities.anchor: The Gateway Arch in St Louis (1965)
activities.caption: pair each builder with what they shaped
activities.name: archFormMatch

config.prompt: Hooke's inversion still earns its keep. Match each to the geometry they used:

pairs.right: weighted chains hung upside down, letting gravity compute compression-only geometry
a flattened, weighted catenary in stainless steel at monument scale
concrete graded from heavy basalt at the base to featherweight pumice at the top
long spans in concrete centimetres thick, limited only by the cost of the moulds

config.why: The Gateway Arch stands because every section pushes on the next. Every one of these is the same idea: find the shape where forces flow without bending.

activities.anchor: Steel is strong in tension, so beams could span far
activities.caption: order the escape from the wall
activities.name: archSkyscraperOrder

config.prompt: The canon answers one question five ways: how does load reach the ground? Order the rise of the framed building:
items: Load-bearing masonry governs for five millennia — openings weaken walls, height is capped by the mortar's crushing strength
The arch, vault and dome escape the span limit of a plain stone lintel
Gothic flying buttresses catch the vault's sideways thrust and route it outside, so walls become curtain
The safety elevator (Otis, 1850s) makes height habitable
The steel skeleton frame (Chicago, 1885) lets frames stack floor upon floor and walls hang off as skin
config.why: Steel is strong in tension, so beams could span far. The skyscraper became possible because the frame took over the load and the wall was released to be glass.

activities.anchor: The two are partners because they
activities.caption: true or false — the composites and the canon
activities.name: archCompositeJudge

statements.s: Concrete and steel are partners because they expand at nearly the same rate with heat.
statements.why: And because the alkaline concrete protects the steel from rust — two virtues in one composite.

statements.s: The arch holds because mortar glues the stones together.
statements.why: It holds by geometry. Cut the mortar away and a well-built arch can still stand, each wedge-shaped voussoir locked by compression.

statements.s: Load-bearing masonry capped building height at the mortar's crushing strength.
statements.why: Hence the thick, small-windowed architecture of fortresses and old churches.

statements.s: An arch can survive having its shape altered as long as no stone is removed.
statements.why: The shape IS the load path. What an arch cannot survive is having that shape altered.

activities.anchor: embodied carbon has
activities.caption: guess concrete's share of global emissions
activities.name: archCementEstimate

config.prompt: Roughly what percentage of global CO₂ emissions comes from cement alone?
config.why: About 7–8 percent — so embodied carbon has moved from sustainability footnote to design driver, a first-order criterion alongside maintenance, durability and fire.
config.context: One material, one eighth of the planet's emissions — which is why mass timber and retrofit-first design are no longer niche.

activities.anchor: ceiling tie
activities.caption: trace a load path or misread one
activities.name: archLoadPathBranch

config.root: You are renovating a two-storey house and want to remove an interior wall to open up the ground floor.

choices.label: Is the wall load-bearing — is it on the path?
choices.feedback: Every renovation begins by asking which members are on the path (untouchable) and which are mere infill (removable).

choices.label: Is the wall attractive enough to keep?
choices.feedback: Aesthetics is the second question. The first one can bring the roof down.

taste.text: You have answered a structural question with a design preference. If it was carrying the ceiling joists, the answer is now a collapsed floor.

path.text: The roof's rafters lean on each other — a primitive arch whose spreading thrust is caught by a ceiling tie in tension. The tie's load lands on walls, walls on footing, footing on soil, which is weak in everything but compression and is the ultimate bottom of every path.

config.why: The honest designer can trace every kilogram from its point of application to the earth. That chain is the load path — the single idea every structural drawing is secretly about.

activities.anchor: That stamp is the whole point
activities.caption: bet on what the license actually buys
activities.name: archStampPredict

config.q: What does the licensed architect's stamp and seal legally certify?
choices: That the building will not exceed its budget
That the design is beautiful enough to build
That a person the state has checked for education, supervised experience and examined competence stands behind the documents and is personally accountable
That the contractor has been approved to work from these drawings
config.why: The public cannot audit the safety of a building any more than it can audit a surgeon, so the state licenses the profession. Architecture, like medicine and law, is a licensed profession.

activities.anchor:
But in the United States the
  title is legally protected
activities.caption: true or false — the protected title
activities.name: archTitleJudge

statements.s: Anyone who designs buildings is an architect.
statements.why: In the US the title is legally protected: calling yourself an architect or offering architectural services without a license is against the law.

statements.s: Unlicensed designers do real, legitimate work.
statements.why: Architectural designers, drafters and building designers often do excellent work — they simply cannot use the protected title or take legal responsibility for construction documents.

statements.s: Nobody calls a nurse a doctor, and the parallel to architecture is exact.
statements.why: Both are skilled roles beside a licensed one, which is why the everyday-English looseness about 'architect' matters.

statements.s: Calling yourself an architect without a license is a harmless informality.
statements.why: It breaches the legal protection that exists precisely so the public knows a stamped drawing carries an accountable professional behind it.

activities.anchor: The D.Arch
activities.caption: file each degree by who it suits
activities.name: archDegreeBuckets

config.prompt: Three degree types clear gate one. File each by the student it fits:
buckets: M.Arch — the late decider or career-changer

items.label: about five years, entered straight from secondary school — fastest education gate
after any first degree; three to three and a half years without a design background
front-loads commitment in exchange for finishing education soonest
feeds the profession with people who first studied literature, biology or economics
currently offered in Hawaii

config.why: What the accredited degree certifies is not just design talent but the full professional curriculum — structures, building systems, history, professional practice — which is why a non-accredited degree, however beautiful the portfolio, does not open the same doors.

activities.anchor: The third gate is the ARE
activities.caption: file each requirement under its gate
activities.name: archGateBuckets

config.prompt: Each gate checks a different thing. File each requirement under the gate that tests it:

items.label: a NAAB-accredited degree audited against the profession's standards
3,740 supervised hours across six practice areas
six ARE 5.0 divisions within a five-year rolling window
case-study questions asking what a competent licensed architect would do

config.why: No gate substitutes for another. An intern who spends three years only producing renderings has not been let near construction sites, contracts or code research — and the AXP refuses to call that ready.

activities.anchor: The final grant, though, always comes last
activities.caption: find the faulty line in the career path
activities.name: archPathSpot

config.prompt: A student plans the licensure path. One line is wrong — find it.
lines: The degree is gate one of four: accredited education, supervised experience, examination, licensure.
AXP hours can begin during school, which is one of the two big accelerators in the system.
ARE divisions may be taken in any order within a five-year rolling window.
Finishing an accredited architecture degree makes you an architect, since the degree is the endpoint in most careers.
The final grant always comes last and comes from one place: the state board.
config.correction: The degree is gate one of FOUR — after graduation come 3,740 AXP hours and six exam divisions before any state board will stamp anything with your name.
config.why: The graduate is an 'architectural designer' or intern architect in professional terms. The contrast with licensed engineering is instructive: the same two-stage logic exists there, but architecture adds the logged-experience gate because its failure modes are building-scale and physical.

activities.anchor: sets its own rules around the national requirements
activities.caption: drag between national and state
activities.name: archTwoLevelCompare

config.prompt: A two-level system. Drag the divider.

before.label: national uniformity — what competence means
before.text: NAAB accredits the schools, NCARB runs the experience programme, and ARE 5.0's six divisions are the same everywhere. One vetting of competence serves all boards.

after.label: state authority — who may practise where
after.text: Each jurisdiction licenses for itself, sets its own rules around the national requirements, and holds the disciplinary power to fine, suspend or revoke. Practising in a state without its license breaches that state's law.

config.why: The NCARB Certificate exists precisely to make multi-state practice routine — one vetting, many boards — but each grant is still individual, and firms with national work employ architects licensed in the states they build in.

activities.anchor:
travel far beyond the stamped
    drawing
activities.caption: file each career by whether it stamps
activities.name: archCareerBuckets

config.prompt: The license gates one specific career. File these roles by their relation to the stamp:

items.label: healthcare, housing and adaptive-reuse specialists accountable for stamped documents
BIM and computational design specialists running the profession's software
construction administrator and cost estimator
game and film environment art — worlds are architecture with different physics
real estate development, where reading a building's feasibility is the job

config.why: The education is a general-purpose instrument for the built world, and plenty of its strongest practitioners never stamp a drawing.

activities.anchor: Most things a designer gets wrong
activities.caption: fill the numbers that gate the profession
activities.name: archNumbersCloze

config.text: Gate one is a degree accredited by the %%0%%. Gate two is %%1%% supervised hours across six practice areas. Gate three is the six divisions of ARE 5.0, taken within a five-year %%2%% window.
config.hint: The accrediting board's acronym; the AXP hour total; and the kind of five-year window the exam divisions run within.
